s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic, violaceous, annular skin lesions in a localized area
salient_findings: Discrete, dark red, circular lesions in the right axilla
Severe pruritus at the lesion sites
Lesions are well-circumscribed, violaceous, and annular without scale or erosion
key_facts: Lesions are limited to the right axilla
Severe pruritus wakes the patient up at night
No recent trauma or history of similar lesions
No associated pain, blisters, or systemic symptoms
No improvement with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, or discontinuation of underarm deodorant
Biopsy findings show lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of discrete, dark red, circular lesions with severe pruritus, limited to the right axilla, along with biopsy findings showing lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction, is most consistent with annular lichen planus.

rejected.label: granuloma annulare
rejected.why: Typically presents with papular lesions in a ring-like pattern, often on the hands or feet, which doesn't match this patient's presentation.

rejected.label: atopic dermatitis
rejected.why: Usually involves more widespread lesions and a history of atopy, which this patient does not have.

rejected.label: contact dermatitis
rejected.why: The lack of improvement after discontinuation of underarm deodorant and the specific, localized nature of the lesions make this less likely.

rejected.label: psoriasis
rejected.why: Characterized by scaly, erythematous plaques, which are not described in this patient's presentation.
